newsitem.title: UK: Metals drift back on LME, pre-market sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Metals drift back on LME, pre-market sluggish.

text.p: Early Tuesday trading in LME base metals was slow, with prices drifting back after a slightly steadier start.
Monday's higher price levels were not followed through with any consistency, and with copper stocks showing a small rise the market tripped lower.
"The market as a whole is just drifting - there is not any momentum," one trader said.
Copper stocks rose by 525 tonnes, an inventory increase deemed disappointing after Monday saw a resumption of stock falls.
Three months prices touched an early high of $2,415 a tonne, helped by background support from storms causing power cuts in Chile.
But the market then settled back under some liquidation and profit-taking. Recent trade was at $2,410, up just $1 from Monday's kerb close.
In the short term the market is likely to be capped by interim resistance around $2,415 prior to the more important target at $2,440 - the 1997 high.
Copper's languid performance had a knock-on impact on other base metals, with aluminium sliding back to $1,660, a $10 loss.
A 3,150-tonne LME warehouse stock fall followed Monday's 2,600 tonne decline, but was shrugged off to some extent as inventory drawdowns are now the norm.
Tin came under pressure during the pre-market after a 180-tonne stock rise, and prices slid back to $5,800, triggering sell-stops down to $5,760. Last trade was at $5,770, down $100.

Nickel dipped as well, and was $95 lower at $7,740. News that Russian exports from Dudinka were being held up, due to floods, came as no surprise, as this is the usual occurrence at this time of the year.
Zinc dropped back from Monday's 4-1/2 year highs, despite a 2,400-tonne stock fall, and was $7 easier at $1,328. Lead was marked down to $622/625, against $630 last on Monday.
Alloy was trading quietly at a steady $1,525 a tonne.
